# program.json

The JSON Schema in [schemas/program.json](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/schemas/program.json), as a reference.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `programName` | `string` | yes | matches `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`. |
| `functions` | [`functionUnit`](#def-functionunit)[] | yes | Ordered lowest layer first. Each function is one small Dijkstra layer: it may only call functions in strictly lower layers. at least 1 items. |

No other property is allowed.

## Definitions

<a id="def-expr"></a>

### `expr`

An vector-lang expression node. Pure, total (except division), no loops, no recursion.

One or more of:

- [an object `kind "num"`](#def-expr-kind-num)
- [an object `kind "bool"`](#def-expr-kind-bool)
- [an object `kind "var"`](#def-expr-kind-var)
- [an object `kind "unop"`](#def-expr-kind-unop)
- [an object `kind "binop"`](#def-expr-kind-binop)
- [an object `kind "ite"`](#def-expr-kind-ite)
- [an object `kind "call"`](#def-expr-kind-call)

<a id="def-expr-kind-num"></a>

#### `kind "num"`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"num"` | yes |  |
| `value` | `string` | yes | Numeric literal as a plain decimal string, e.g. "0.91" or "-3". Never scientific notation, never a JSON number — the string reaches the solver as an exact rational. matches `^-?(0\|[1-9]\d*)(\.\d+)?$`. |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-expr-kind-unop"></a>

#### `kind "unop"`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"unop"` | yes |  |
| `op` | `"not"` \| `"neg"` \| `"abs"` \| `"floor"` \| `"ceil"` | yes | not: Bool→Bool. neg/abs: numeric→same type. floor/ceil: Real→Real (round toward -inf / +inf; the result is integer-valued but stays Real). |
| `arg` | [`expr`](#def-expr) | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-expr-kind-binop"></a>

#### `kind "binop"`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"binop"` | yes |  |
| `op` | `"+"` \| `"-"` \| `"*"` \| `"/"` \| `"min"` \| `"max"` \| `"<"` \| `"<="` \| `">"` \| `">="` \| `"=="` \| `"!="` \| `"and"` \| `"or"` \| `"implies"` | yes | Arithmetic (+ - * /), min/max (both operands numeric, same type), comparisons, and boolean logic. `/` requires Real operands and yields Real (use Real, not Int, for division). Every Int `+`, `-` and `*` the emitted code evaluates must provably stay within ±(2^53−1), where a float64 holds every integer exactly; one that may leave it is a range hazard. Prefer linear arithmetic: multiply variables by literal constants, not by other variables — nonlinear terms can make the solver return unknown. |
| `left` | [`expr`](#def-expr) | yes |  |
| `right` | [`expr`](#def-expr) | yes |  |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-ty"></a>

### `ty`

`"Real"` \| `"Int"` \| `"Bool"`

<a id="def-clause"></a>

### `clause`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axiomId` | `string` | yes | The id of the spec-plan axiom this clause formalizes, e.g. "AX1" or "AX-RATE" (letters, digits, _ and - only — the id is embedded in emitted source). Every axiom in the spec plan must be enforced by at least one clause. matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`. |
| `expr` | [`expr`](#def-expr) | yes | A Bool-typed expression over the parameters (and `result` in ensures). |

No other property is allowed.

<a id="def-functionunit"></a>

### `functionUnit`

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | matches `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`. |
| `layer` | `integer` | yes | at least 1. |
| `purpose` | `string` | yes | One plain-language sentence. |
| `params` | [object[]](#def-functionunit-params) | yes |  |
| `returnType` | [`ty`](#def-ty) | yes |  |
| `requires` | [`clause`](#def-clause)[] | yes | Preconditions. "Throws/errors if X" in the spec means a precondition of NOT X — the emitted code enforces it with a runtime throw. |
| `ensures` | [`clause`](#def-clause)[] | yes | Postconditions over the parameters and `result`. Proven by the solver for ALL inputs satisfying the preconditions. at least 1 items. |
| `body` | [`expr`](#def-expr) | yes | A single pure expression matching returnType. No `result` here. |

No other property is allowed.
